title: Microsoft Purview DSPM: item-level investigation and remediation of overshared SharePoint items in data risk assessments (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the app-permissions control gives roles that cannot grant the Microsoft Graph application permissions it describes. App registration and permission selection are documented for those roles, but granting these permissions requires Privileged Role Administrator or an appropriately authorized custom role; the endpoint itself is valid.

claims.quote: Users are empowered to remediate overshared items by resolving, notifying, applying a sensitivity label, or removing sharing links for selected item(s).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout, register app and grant consent
claims.claim: Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator can perform the Graph application-permission grant described in the control.
claims.quote: Privileged Role Administrator - the least privileged role supported for Microsoft Graph and Azure AD Graph app roles
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence in controls[0].note with 'App registration and permission selection need Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator; granting Microsoft Graph application permissions needs Privileged Role Administrator or a custom role authorized for those permissions.' Make the same distinction in the Before rollout bullet. The DSPM prerequisite page lists app-configuration roles, but the cited Graph reference qualifies grants of Microsoft Graph app roles; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent explicitly excludes Microsoft Graph application permissions from Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator consent authority.

claims.fix: The app-secret review instruction has no corresponding control row. Narrow that After rollout bullet to 'Review the app's Graph permissions on a schedule.' Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
